Surface plot

Simple Table Spine

  1. Accept the contract.
  2. Receive the sealed package.
  3. Enter the old forest.
  4. Find the wrecked cart.
  5. Face the Strixwolf Mother.
  6. Survive or resolve the Bramble Union ambush.
  7. Deliver the Keystone Asset to Hush.
  8. Help the Custodian install the wardstone.
  9. Defend Open Vale until the ward renews.

Concealed pressure

Perceived vs. True Antagonist

Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end.

Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy.

SZ-00 · Ready to Start / Table Frame

Welcome to the Goldspire Messengers

Establish tone, expectations, and the table's shared social contract.

Player-facing: This is a beginner-friendly Daggerheart one-shot. You do not need to know the rules ahead of time. We will learn by playing.

Player Display Points

  • Session Zero mode selected

  • Handouts visible

SZ-00B · Welcome, Logistics, and GM Role

Welcome to the table

Cover room logistics, the GM role, the player role, and the shape of an in-person one-shot before teaching rules.

Player-facing: This is a standalone one-shot at Mox. We are here to tell a complete story tonight, learn the game as we go, and make sure everyone has enough information to participate comfortably.

Player Display Points
  • Your GM is Kyle, he/him. Kyle has 15+ years running in-person and online TTRPGs.
  • GM style for Daggerheart: story-first, roleplay-friendly, and mechanics in service of the table's fun.
  • Kyle plays the world, keeps the rules moving, asks questions, and helps everyone get spotlight.
  • You play one character. Say what they try to do, ask questions, and make choices from their point of view.
  • We will confirm session length, end time, breaks, bathrooms, drinks, and any Mox house policies before we begin.
  • Phones are fine for reference or emergencies. Please keep attention at the table when another player has the spotlight.
  • This is a complete story tonight: Session Zero, opening job, rising trouble, final pressure, and a short closeout if time allows.
TopicTable Version
GM roleKyle plays the world and helps the table move.
Player roleDescribe what your character does and ask questions.
LogisticsTime, breaks, bathrooms, drinks, phones, and Mox policies.
GM Script

Welcome everyone by name if possible. Say: I'm Kyle, he/him, and you can call me Kyle. I've been running TTRPGs for 15+ years, both in person and online. For Daggerheart, my style is story-first and roleplay-friendly: the mechanics are here to support the table's fun and help us resolve risky moments, not to make you memorize a rulebook. I play the world, frame scenes, make rulings, and help everyone get time in the spotlight. You play one character and tell me what they try to do. Before we begin, let's confirm end time, breaks, bathrooms, drinks, phone expectations, and any Mox house policies.

GM Notes
GM Checklist
  • Introduce yourself as GM
  • Name/pronouns: Kyle, he/him
  • Mention 15+ years running in-person and online TTRPGs
  • State story-first, roleplay-friendly Daggerheart style
  • Confirm headcount, seats, names, and any latecomers
  • Confirm session length and target end time
  • Cover Mox house policies or ask staff if needed
  • Point out bathrooms, drinks, and table logistics
  • Set phone policy: reference and emergencies are fine, attention stays at the table
  • State that tonight is a standalone complete story
GM Notes
  • This card exists before safety and rules so strangers know what room they are in.
  • Keep it practical. The table needs confidence, not a speech.
GM-Only / Do Not Project
  • Ask May or Mox staff for current house policies before the event if they are not already posted.

SZ-01 · Concept, Aim, Tone, Subject Matter

What kind of game is this?

Clarify Concept, Aim, Tone, and Subject Matter before play begins.

Player-facing: We are playing a fantasy delivery job in the Goldspire Territories: dangerous roads, strange magic, communities under pressure, and corporations trying to turn everything into paperwork.

Player Display Points
  • Concept: a corporate-fantasy delivery job that becomes morally complicated.
  • Aim: learn Daggerheart, build the party, protect a community, and discover what the sealed delivery means.
  • Tone: mostly sincere fantasy adventure, with corporate satire and dark whimsy around the edges.
  • Subject matter: fantasy danger, animal peril, ambush, death, corporate exploitation, undead, and memory or fear magic.
  • We can pause, soften, veil, or redirect content.

Concept: Corporate-fantasy delivery incident in the Goldspire Territories.

Aim: Learn Daggerheart, protect a community, and discover what the sealed delivery means.

Tone: 70% sincere fantasy, 20% corporate satire, 10% dark whimsy.

Subject Matter
  • animal danger
  • ambush
  • death
  • corporate exploitation
  • undead
  • memory/fear magic
GM Script

Name the Concept, Aim, Tone, and Subject Matter without using the acronym as shorthand. Ask whether anything in the subject matter list needs a line, veil, or softer framing.

GM Notes
GM Checklist
  • Concept explained
  • Aim explained
  • Tone explained
  • Subject matter checked
GM Notes
  • CATS means Concept, Aim, Tone, Subject Matter. Expand it on first use.

SZ-01B · Rating / Content Notes

Content rating

Set a clear rating and content frame before safety tools.

Player-facing: Think adult PG-13-ish fantasy adventure. There will be combat and danger, but violence descriptions stay light unless the table chooses to make a moment more intense.

Player Display Points
  • This is an adult game, but not a grimdark or graphic game.
  • Likely content: combat, peril, ambushes, monsters, undead, corporate exploitation, fear or memory magic, and morally complicated choices.
  • Animal peril may appear. Violence against animals is optional and can be softened, avoided, or redirected.
  • If anything I describe or any action at the table makes you uncomfortable, say pause, slow down, rewind, or break.
  • The goal is to explore fantasy danger together while keeping the real table safe and communicative.
ContentDefault
CombatPresent, described lightly.
Animal perilOptional; can be softened or avoided.
Horror/undeadAtmospheric, not graphic.
GM Script

Frame the one-shot as adult PG-13-ish. Say that combat exists, descriptions of violence will be light, animal peril can be avoided or softened, and any player can pause or redirect if something crosses a line.

GM Notes
GM Checklist
  • Adult PG-13-ish rating explained
  • Combat and light violence expectations explained
  • Optional animal peril explained
  • Pause/redirect permission reinforced
GM Notes
  • Do not over-explain the content warning. Make it clear, quick, and normal.
  • Use the safety page for extra tools only if the table seems to need them.
GM-Only / Do Not Project
  • Module contains possible animal peril, combat against conscious beings, monsters, undead, exploitation, and fear/memory magic.

Tonight's shape

SZ-02 · Safety Tools / Table Agreement

Safety tools

Establish safety tools and participation norms.

Player-facing: You do not need to justify a boundary. If something is not fun, too intense, or not for tonight, we can pause, redirect, fade to black, or move on.

Player Display Points
  • Open Door: you can step away at any point and return when ready.
  • Simple table signal: say pause, slow down, can we rewind, or break.
  • If you missed something, ask me to repeat it.
  • If I am moving too fast, ask me to slow down.
  • If you are confused, ask any question at any time. There are no dumb questions here.
  • If a topic is okay in the story but not for your character, say not for me.
  • Discord or text can help between scenes, but I may not see it immediately while running the table.
SignalMeaning
PauseStop for a quick check-in or redirect.
Slow downRepeat, clarify, or make more room.
BreakTake five minutes away from the table.
Safety Tools
  • Open Door
  • Pause / slow down / rewind / break
  • Lines and Veils if needed
  • Not For Me, Thanks if needed
  • Stars and Wishes at the end if time allows
GM Script

Before we play, I want to keep safety and communication simple. You can step away at any point, ask for a break, ask me to slow down or repeat something, or say pause if something is uncomfortable or confusing. I may talk too fast or interrupt sometimes; you are welcome to interrupt me, ask any question, or tell me to rewind. The story is for everyone at the table.

GM Notes
GM Checklist
  • Lines and veils explained
  • Simple pause/slow down/break signal explained
  • Open Door explained
  • Break policy explained
  • Shared table responsibility explained
  • Safety intake reviewed if used
GM Notes
  • Keep private lines/veils and intake responses hidden from player display.
  • Default to lightweight in-person tools for a four-to-five-player one-shot.
  • Optional deeper tools live on the safety page for GM use only if needed.
  • If no Google Form URL is configured, show a missing-link note in GM view rather than inventing one.
GM-Only / Do Not Project
  • Private lines and veils text area
  • Safety intake responses
  • Only sanitized summary may be exported

SZ-02B · Player Expectations / Shared Table Care

How we make this fun together

Set player expectations for participation, shared care, questions, and communication.

Player-facing: This works best when everyone is engaged, respectful, and helping the table have fun. You are responsible for your own fun and for noticing the other people at the table too.

Player Display Points
  • Engage with the story and ask questions.
  • Invite other players in: ask them what their character thinks, notices, or does.
  • Speak when it is your turn, and be mindful of how much space you are taking.
  • Only participate at the level you are comfortable with.
  • Tell me if you are confused, uncomfortable, not having fun, or need help.
  • I will do my best to engage everyone, but the table works because we all pay attention to each other.
  • If there is time at the end, we may do quick Stars and Wishes: one thing you liked, one thing you would want more or different next time.
ExpectationMeaning
AskQuestions are welcome at any time.
ShareMake space for other players.
SignalTell the GM what you need.
GM Script

Set the social expectation directly: this is not only my responsibility as GM. Everyone helps the story work by engaging, listening, asking questions, and making space. Tell players they can interrupt you to ask for help, a repeat, a slower pace, or a pause.

GM Notes
GM Checklist
  • Participation expectations explained
  • Questions welcome at any time
  • Shared responsibility named
  • Stars and Wishes previewed briefly
GM Notes
  • Keep this brief. It should feel like permission and care, not a lecture.
  • Mention Stars and Wishes only as an end-of-session possibility.

SZ-03 · Daggerheart Rules Snapshot

How Daggerheart works

Teach the minimum Daggerheart rules needed to begin.

Player-facing: Daggerheart is narrative fantasy. The GM describes the world, players describe what their characters do, and we roll when the outcome is risky, uncertain, or dramatic.

Player Display Points
  • Describe what your character tries to do.
  • If it is risky or uncertain, roll Hope and Fear d12s.
  • Add the trait that fits your approach.
  • Tell the GM the total and whether Hope or Fear was higher.
  • We will learn the rest as it matters.
Progressive Player Display Beats
  • Overview: Daggerheart is a story-first fantasy game. Describe your action first; the rules help when the moment is risky, uncertain, or dramatic.
  • TTRPG basics: You and the GM are telling a story together. You play one character. The GM plays the world. Dice decide risky or uncertain moments, and there is no single win condition.
  • Duality Dice: Most action rolls use two d12s: one Hope die and one Fear die. Add the right trait, compare to the difficulty, and tell the GM whether Hope or Fear was higher.
  • Outcomes: Success and failure matter, and Hope or Fear tells us the direction of the next beat.
  • Different from D&D: Daggerheart still feels like fantasy adventure, but the table listens for story momentum as much as pass/fail math.
  • Sheet rules: The sheet is a menu of options, not homework. Use the parts you need when they become relevant.
  • During play: Say what your character wants, tries, asks, notices, or risks. If you freeze, say that, and the table will help you find an option.
Rules Terms
GM Script

Teach only the minimum rules, then move on. Open the GM Rules Drawer for deeper questions, but do not dump the full rulebook before play.

GM Notes
GM Checklist
  • Duality Dice explained
  • Hope/Fear explained
  • Experiences explained
  • Helping explained
  • Outcome matrix explained
GM Notes
  • Every rules term should link to the GM Rules Drawer in GM view.
  • Do not present non-official or stale mechanics as official Daggerheart rules.

SZ-04 · Character Selection / Sheet Orientation

Your character sheet

Choose pregens, orient players to character sheets, and preserve Marlowe or a chosen replacement PC as the crew's package custody holder without making any PC the sole job-giver.

Player-facing: In front of you: a character sheet, quick rules card, connection sheet, and safety card. Your sheet tells you who your character is, what they are good at, what they can do, and how much pressure or harm they can take.

Player Display Points
  • Look for: name and vibe, traits, Experiences, weapons/actions, Hope, Stress, Hit Points, Armor, and class/domain abilities.
  • Pick or confirm a character. If you chose ahead of time, make sure the sheet in front of you matches that choice.
  • Marlowe Fairwind - playable Loreborne Elf Sorcerer pregen and default package custodian; she receives the job with the crew.
  • Barnacle - sneaky rogue with questionable logistics instincts.
  • Garrick Reed - kind ex-security warrior.
  • Khari Nix - giant guardian loyal to people before contracts.
  • Varian Soto - sharp-eyed ranger tracking unlicensed apex fauna.
MotiveHook
MoneyI need the money.
DebtI owe someone in the crew.
SuspicionI distrust Emeris and want to know what this is.
CommunityI know Hush, the village, or Old Sable, the forest route.
Progressive Player Display Beats
  • Sheet overview: Your sheet is the fast map of who you are, what you are good at, and what pressure you can take.
  • Rolls: Describe the action first. If it is risky, uncertain, or dramatic, the GM will ask for a roll.
  • Abilities: Your printed sheet and cards tell you what special things your character can do.
  • Choose: Pick a sheet, confirm it matches your seat or registry choice, and choose a reason this character accepted the job.

Required Decision: Marlowe PC / unplayed pregen / reskinned PC; assign the package custodian function if needed

GM Script

Tell players what is physically in front of them and point to each major sheet area. Marlowe stays a PC and default package custodian unless replaced; Sabine can be used in the Prologue only as an optional backup NPC job-giver. Either way, everyone receives the job together.

GM Notes
GM Checklist
  • Characters selected
  • Marlowe PC or chosen package custodian status assigned
  • Handouts confirmed
GM Notes
  • Quick mode: use pregens as written.
  • Guided mode: rename, pronouns, look, motive, and equivalent Experience label only.
  • Do not change stats, damage, cards, class features, or balance during a short public slot.
GM-Only / Do Not Project
  • What PCs do not know: ward function, soul-economy implications, Bramble Union motives, final ritual threat, Relay Spire hook.

SZ-06 · Connections Workshop

Build connections

Build relationships between PCs.

Player-facing: Offer, don't overwrite. A connection prompt is your character's perspective: what they remember, saw, believed, misunderstood, felt, or interpreted.

Player Display Points
  • The other player can accept it, clarify it, complicate it, soften it, or pass.
  • Yes, and...
  • Yes, but...
  • Can we soften that?
  • I like the emotional idea, but not that detail.
  • Pass; give me another prompt.
  • Active prompt: Which PC knows why you really accepted this contract?
Progressive Player Display Beats
  • How it works: A connection prompt is a memory one character offers to another player. The other player answers from their character's point of view.
  • Permission: Use plain table language if a prompt needs adjustment.
  • Example: Marlowe asks another PC: I owe you a favor. What happened, and why has Marlowe not paid it back yet?
  • Active prompt: Which PC knows why you really accepted this contract?

Principle: Offer, don't overwrite.

GM Script

Use the prompt bank and Connection Builder. Ask each player for at least one connection in quick mode. Save accepted, clarified, complicated, or passed results.

GM Notes
GM Checklist
  • At least one connection target per player
  • Connection Builder entries saved
  • Group memory asked if time allows
  • Ask one optional world-connection question per player if the table has energy.
  • Log answers as table-contributed canon when they point at a faction, NPC, or location.
GM Notes
  • Process: character postcards, one anchor connection, one tension/trust connection, then one group memory.
  • Show players only the active prompt and permission language, not the whole GM prompt bank.

SZ-07 · What PCs Know

What your characters know

Align starting knowledge without leaking hidden information.

Player-facing: You are on a delivery job to the village of Hush. The cargo is sealed, valuable, and not supposed to be opened without permission.

Player Display Points
  • You are escorting one sealed cargo unit.
  • It is important, guarded, and not supposed to be opened without permission.
  • It is going to Hush, a village in the Goldspire Territories.
  • The route crosses Sablewood Logistics Preserve: a vast fantasy forest, called Old Sable by some locals.
  • Payment follows verified delivery.
  • You begin inside the system: loyal, ignorant, conflicted, pragmatic, or simply hired.
GM Script

Read the player-safe starting knowledge. Keep the hidden facts in GM view only and use them for foreshadowing, not for projection.

Class / Ancestry / Community Reveals
  • Loreborne or Knowledge-focused PCs can read the institutional layer.
  • Wildborne/community-focused PCs can read local custom and ecological stress.
  • Martial/security-focused PCs can read threat posture and custody logic.
  • Magic-focused PCs can feel ward tone, soul-signal, or spell instability.
  • Loreborne: spots older legal, heraldic, or ward-craft language under the branding.

  • Highborne: reads etiquette, class panic, and reputational risk.
  • Ridgeborne: notices stonework, weight, pressure, and structural weakness.
  • Wildborne: reads the land, animals, and local ecological stress.
  • Elf/Ribbet/Human/Giant/Katari: invite one sensory or social detail from the player's heritage.
  • Sorcerer/Rogue/Warrior/Guardian/Ranger: give each class one table-facing way to shine without changing the plot.

How to Spend Fear Here
  • Make the contact catch a PC reading her and go guarded.

Emeris clerk: Routine route assurance. The form says routine, and forms are paid to be optimistic.

S01-02 · The Overturned Vendor Cart

The party finds a vendor cart blocking the road, with spilled produce, invoices, and a useless incident placard.

Manufactured-threat seeds

Seed, Do Not Reveal

Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end.

KEEP EARNED

The driver died from a cut throat; the strixwolf did not kill him.

Roll / gate: Instinct or Knowledge Medium 15

ADD EARNED

Near the cart is a pre-written Grail "Hazard Confirmed: Strixwolf Attack" tag.

Roll / gate: Finesse or Instinct Medium 15

Skip the staged-bramble earned seed; move to ambush sooner.

Action RollOfficialFive Roll OutcomesOfficialInstinctOfficialKnowledgeOfficialFinesseOfficialExperiencesOfficialRoll SliderAdaptation

This is the first crack in the official story. The route promised safety, but the cart is ruined, the driver is dead, and the system’s response is decorative. Run this scene as threshold into branded wilderness and first moral test: The overturned cart gives the party a mystery before it gives them a fight. Keep the camera close to practical choices, visible consequences, and the difference between ordinary people and the infrastructure pressing on them.

GM Details

The placard can be a standard route-monitoring glyph, not proof that anyone meaningfully knows what happened.

Keep player-facing information actionable. Reveal systemic truth through objects, reactions, and consequences before naming it.

Sablewood route lore: this is an approved path, and the body/cart disruption should feel like a coverage failure as much as a wilderness event.

Manufactured-threat lens: seed the contradiction, do not explain it. The surface goal stays simple and heroic.

Loot / Search
  • Use Vendor Cart and Tamsin Vell search tables
  • Keystone Asset™: Inside the sealed crate, packed in wax-paper and reassurance, sits a heavy grey stone the size of a loaf, warm to the touch, faintly humming, with a light deep inside it that is slowly going out.
  • Incident Response Placard™: A flat brass disc on a post holds a watchful glyph and a single cheerful bell. When trouble happens nearby, the glyph lights, the bell rings once, brightly, and then nothing else happens at all.
  • Sableblade: Growing straight up out of dark forest soil, like a sapling that decided to be a sword, is a blade of living dark wood and pale metal. It has no maker's mark and hums when your hand nears the hilt.
  • Recall Stone: A smooth grey pebble feels warm and ordinary until it refuses to stay where you put it. Set it down, look away, and it waits back in your palm.
  • Goldwater Liability Token™: A heavy brass chit with a smiling coin-face drops into your palm like a tiny verdict. The fine print is too small to read without feeling blamed.
  • Tamsin's Home-Token: A small thumb-polished token on a cord hangs beside the torn blue scarf, warm from wear and etched with a tiny house mark instead of a company seal.
  • Cracked Pocket Ward™: A cheap little ward charm sits cracked down the middle, still trying to glow through a smiling warranty sticker.

S02-03 · Bramble Union Ambush

Bramble Union reclaimers attack the carriage to seize the cargo.

Manufactured-threat seeds

Seed, Do Not Reveal

Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end.

REFLAVOR GUARANTEED

The reclaimers target the cargo and manifest, not purses, and avoid killing when possible.

REFLAVOR GUARANTEED

Their gear includes salvaged, repainted Grail/Kazrak kit: ex-workers, not feral bandits.

Roll / gate: Knowledge Medium 15 to name the issue

ADD EARNED

"That stone belongs in the ground." "You do not know what you are carrying."

1:30 Act 2: Bramble ambush

Abstract the fight via a Group Action roll; keep one captured reclaimer for the interrogation seed.

SpotlightOfficialAdversary AttacksOfficialDamage RollsRules CanonEvasionOfficialDamage ThresholdsOfficialArmor SlotsOfficialFearOfficialRestrainedOfficialDisposition / Resolution TrackAdaptation

The Bramble Union are the immediate antagonists, but they are desperate rather than cartoon evil. They are dangerous, armed, and under pressure. Run this scene as external opposition and morally complicated conflict: The Bramble Union ambush should feel dangerous and understandable at the same time. Keep the camera close to practical choices, visible consequences, and the difference between ordinary people and the infrastructure pressing on them.

Loot / Search
  • Use Bramble Union Ambushers and Claimrunner loot tables
  • Bramble Union Stoneweave: A garment of thousands of tiny polished stones moves like cloth and turns thorns like armor. Every fitted piece looks cut by hands that loved the work.
  • Vial of Briarpowder: A small stoppered vial holds fine grey-green thorn powder that seems to drink the light. A blade edge near it looks sharper and hungrier.
  • Bramble Ward-Scrap Charm Cluster: A knot of blue ward shards, twine, and tiny salvage tags clacks softly at a Bramblefolk belt. It looks illegal only because it looks useful.
  • Claimrunner Serrated Blade: A short serrated blade shows careful filing along the back edge and a handle wrapped in road cord. It is ugly in the practical way of a tool that has never had a decorative day.

S04-04 · The Keystone Reveal

The crate contains the Keystone Asset / ward-stone tied to major protective infrastructure.

Manufactured-threat seeds

Seed, Do Not Reveal

Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end.

KEEP GUARANTEED

The sealed package is the capital's ward Keystone; the city is unwarded while it is away.

ADD SEED

"Your capital's safety is older than your contracts. It is the very thing they teach you to fear."

ADD EARNED

The Keystone's magic is pre-corporate forest-ward work, the same school companies call primitive.

Roll / gate: Knowledge Hard 20

2:40 Act 4: Hanging Office

Compress the reveal; bank the Short Rest into travel narration.

KnowledgeOfficialInstinctOfficialCritical SuccessOfficial

This is the turn. The job was never ordinary. The corporation concealed a ward failure because public knowledge would invite panic, predators, and acquisition. Run this scene as mentor-custodian truth reveal: The Keystone Asset stops being cargo and becomes a communal protection problem. Keep the camera close to practical choices, visible consequences, and the difference between ordinary people and the infrastructure pressing on them.

roll check skill check action rolls with Hope hope spend spend Hope with Fear GM Fear fear spend crit critical doubles

Six Traits

trait traits acrobatics dexterity dodge athletics force grapple stealth sleight of hand control hide tinker perception insight survival animal handling persuasion deception intimidation performance arcana history investigation religion nature
  • Agility: sprint, leap, maneuver.
  • Strength: lift, smash, grapple.
  • Finesse: control, hide, tinker.
  • Instinct: perceive, sense, navigate.
  • Presence: charm, perform, deceive.
  • Knowledge: recall, analyze, comprehend.

GM Screen Edge Cases

group action group action roll group roll team action fate roll chance roll luck roll temporary temporary tag temporary condition temporary effect falling fall damage collision crash dangerous speed spellcast spellcast roll spell roll cast a spell unarmed punch kick improvised punch
  • Group Action: choose a leader; helpers roll reactions; successes and failures shift the leader's roll.
  • Fate Roll: define the stakes, then roll one Duality Die when the outcome is pure chance.
  • Temporary effects: clear through the listed move, natural end, or GM/Fear procedure if a spell says so.
  • Falling or collision: use the SRD damage guide and fit the danger to the fiction.
  • Spellcast Roll: only when a feature calls for the character's Spellcast trait.
  • Unarmed attack: Strength or Finesse, then Proficiency d4 damage on a hit.

#rules-canon

Action Roll Flow

['roll', 'check', 'skill check', 'action rolls'] ['saving throw', 'save', 'reaction'] ['group action', 'group action roll', 'group roll', 'team action']

Ask what the PC does, choose the trait that matches the fictional approach, set or reveal the Difficulty, then roll.

Roll Duality Dice, add the trait and any applicable Experience or bonus, compare the total to the Difficulty, then read Hope/Fear spin.

Roll only when the outcome is uncertain and the consequence matters. If there is no meaningful pressure, give the result without a roll.

#rules-canon

Duality Dice

['2d12', 'hope die', 'fear die']

Official default: roll two d12s, one Hope die and one Fear die.

Total the dice, add the relevant trait and bonuses, then compare to Difficulty.

The higher die determines whether the roll is with Hope or with Fear. Matching dice are a Critical Success.

Reaction rolls use the Duality Dice structure, but they do not generate Hope or Fear.

#rules-canon

Hope/Fear Outcomes

TotalSpinResult
>= DifficultyHopeSuccess with Hope: get what you want and gain Hope.
>= DifficultyFearSuccess with Fear: get what you want, but there is a cost or consequence; GM gains Fear.
< DifficultyHopeFailure with Hope: things do not go as planned, but gain Hope.
< DifficultyFearFailure with Fear: things go badly; major consequence or complication; GM gains Fear.

#rules-canon

Critical Success

['crit', 'critical', 'doubles']

When the Hope die and Fear die match, the roll is a Critical Success.

A Critical Success counts as a roll with Hope even if the total would otherwise miss the Difficulty.

On a Critical Success, the PC gains Hope and clears 1 Stress. On an attack roll, follow the official critical damage rules.

#gm-aid not official

D&D-to-Daggerheart Translation

D&D Conversion

Daggerheart uses traits, not D&D skills. Pick the trait that matches the player's fictional approach.

Use the D&D conversion page as a GM aid for players arriving from 5e; it is not official Daggerheart rules text.

#rules-canon

Advantage / Disadvantage

['advantage', 'disadvantage']

Advantage adds a d6 advantage die to the roll total.

Disadvantage subtracts a d6 disadvantage die from the roll total.

Advantage and disadvantage cancel each other out before rolling. If multiple advantage dice remain, use the highest one.

The GM may grant advantage or disadvantage when the fiction supports it.

#rules-canon

Experiences, Help, Tag Team

Experiences are short backstory/expertise phrases. Spend 1 Hope before a roll to add a relevant Experience modifier.

Help an Ally: spend 1 Hope, describe feasible help, roll a d6 advantage die, and add it to the acting PC's roll using the normal advantage rules.

Tag Team Roll: once per session, spend 3 Hope to combine two PCs' efforts. Both roll, choose one result for both, and resolve as a single action roll.

#rules-canon

Hope Uses / Fear Uses

['with Hope', 'hope spend', 'spend Hope'] ['Sablewood Hope Moments', 'Sablewood Fear Moments', 'hope moments', 'fear moments']

Hope can be spent to Help an Ally, use Experiences, initiate a Tag Team Roll, or activate Hope Features.

On a roll with Fear, the GM gains Fear and makes a move reflecting the complication.

Fear can be spent to spotlight adversaries, use Fear Features, make stronger GM moves, apply adversary Experiences, and advance pressure when the rules or stat block call for it.

#rules-canon

GM Moves / Adversary Spotlight

['GM Move', 'make a move'] ['rules drawer', 'quick reference'] GM MovesAdversary Spotlight

The spotlight moves through the fiction rather than a fixed initiative order.

The GM commonly makes moves when a PC rolls with Fear or fails an action roll.

Use softer moves to telegraph, reveal, or reposition. Use harder moves when the fiction and result call for direct consequence.

Spend Fear or use features when the adversary/environment rules call for it.

#rules-canon

Adversary Attack Rolls

['enemy attack', 'attack roll', 'adversary attack'] Adversary Attack Rolls

Adversaries roll a d20 plus their attack modifier against the target PC's Evasion.

PCs do not roll defense by default. Use reaction rolls only when a rule, feature, or GM call gives one.

PC action rolls against adversaries use the adversary's Difficulty from the stat block.

#rules-canon

Damage / Armor / Stress

['damage', 'threshold', 'thresholds'] ['falling', 'fall damage', 'collision', 'crash', 'dangerous speed'] ['damage die', 'damage dice', 'weapon damage'] Damage / Armor

Compare incoming damage to the character's damage thresholds to determine how many HP are marked.

Mark an Armor Slot to reduce the severity of incoming damage by one threshold.

When a character marks their last Stress, they become Vulnerable until they clear at least 1 Stress.

If a character must mark Stress while all Stress slots are marked, follow the official overflow consequence from the character rules.

#rules-canon

Short Rest

['rest', 'Prepare', 'Tend to Wounds', 'Clear Stress', 'Repair Armor']

A short rest is about an hour to catch breath and recover.

Each PC may swap domain cards between loadout and vault, then choose two moves, including choosing the same move twice.

Short rest moves: Tend to Wounds, Clear Stress, Repair Armor, or Prepare.

Prepare gains Hope; preparing with one or more party members gives each of those PCs 2 Hope.

#rules-canon + module tracker

Countdown

['clock', 'timer', 'countdown']

Countdowns are visible pressure clocks. Tell players what changes when a countdown ticks.

On progress countdowns, successful action rolls can tick the party closer to the goal.

On consequence countdowns, failures or success with Fear can tick the opposing pressure closer.

Open Vale uses a module ritual countdown as a tracker; do not treat it as a new condition.

#rules-canon

Ranges

['range', 'movement', 'distance']

Use Daggerheart range bands at the table: Melee, Very Close, Close, Far, Very Far, and Out of Range.

When exact distance is not important, keep ranges conversational and tied to reachable action.

#rules-canon

Official Conditions

Official Conditions

Daggerheart has three primary global conditions: Hidden, Restrained, and Vulnerable.

Some features create unique effects, but those are feature-specific text, not module-wide conditions.

Unless a rule says otherwise, the same condition cannot stack on one target.

Temporary conditions can be cleared with a fitting action roll, a GM-approved fictional method, or by an adversary spending its spotlight to clear the condition.

Unconscious appears only as Death Move/status context in this Atlas, not as a global condition card.
